name: Marchica Lagoon (Mar Chica)
hero_subtitle: One of the Mediterranean’s great lagoons — calm water, birdlife and the landscape that defines Nador.

overview.title: The water that shapes the city
overview.p1: Marchica — also called Mar Chica — is a vast saltwater lagoon separated from the open Mediterranean by a narrow coastal strip. It is the first thing many visitors notice, and the feature that gives Nador its sense of space.
overview.p2: Walk the edges, watch for seasonal birds including flamingos, and return at sunset when the corniche lights meet the water. Boat or kayak options appear in season with local operators.
overview.p3: It is not a swimming pool: conditions and access points vary. Use it as landscape and evening atmosphere as much as a single “sight”.

food.li1: Corniche seafood grills in the evening.

food.li3: Fresh fish when boats land at Beni Ansar.

food.p2: Cash is useful for smaller lagoon-side stops.

q1.question: Can I swim in the lagoon?
q1.answer: Some edges are used for swimming; always check local conditions. Clearer swimming is often better at open-coast beaches like Charrana.

q2.question: Flamingos?
q2.answer: Seasonal — more likely at certain times of year along quieter shores.

q3.question: Best time of day?
q3.answer: Late afternoon and evening for light and corniche energy.

q4.question: Need a guide?
q4.answer: Not for the main promenade edges; useful for boat segments.

q5.question: How long to spend?
q5.answer: Two to four hours for a first walk and sunset is typical.
